titles.653: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — your imputation also overthrows original vice and God’s φιλανθρωπία
titles.654: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC equity — willed Adam to bear our person in sinning, not in being punished
titles.655: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC equity — head when he sinned; sin loco nostro, not punished loco nostro
titles.656: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC equity — impose our persons for sinning, snatch them lest he be punished loco
titles.657: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Peter Martyr (Calvin/Bucer) mine; sin in Adam by communion, not singular imputation
titles.658: Man. Post. Cap. IX tip — sinned in Adam as we were in him: by natural generation, not divine imputation

latin.653: Non modo autem imputatio quam tueris tollit vitium originale, quod tamen nobis, proh dolor, omnibus & singulis medullitus infixum est, & Scriptura clamat & experientia contestatur, sed ea quoque Dei φιλανθρωπίαν labefactat.
latin.654: Quippe qui voluerit Adamum sustinere personam nostram cum peccavit, non voluerit autem nostram personam eundem sustinere cum punitus est.
latin.655: Consideraverit eum cum peccavit ut caput nostrum, noluerit eum eodem modo considerare cum puniretur: voluerit eum peccare loco nostro, noluerit puniri loco nostro.
latin.656: Nostras personas ei imposuerit ut peccaret loco nostro, ac eodem momento abstulerit ne puniretur itidem loco nostro: perinde ac si nostra ipsorum qui nihil ipsi peccaveramus, morte delectatus fuisset, nihilque aliud illa personarum nostrarum impositione Adamo captasset quam occasionem nos omnes efficiendi peccatores.
latin.657: Quod Petrum Martyrem (qui Calvini & Buceri vestigia secutus totus meus est) ac caeteros dicis agnovisse, omnes homines in Adamo peccasse, mihi non obest, qui clamo omnes homines peccare in Adamo quomodo in Adamo moriuntur, hoc est, vi communionis quam habent cum Adamo, non autem imputatione singularis eius vel peccati, vel mortis.
latin.658: Peccavisse omnes homines in Adamo, quomodo in eo fuerunt. Fuerunt autem in eo non imputatione τοῦ εἶναι ipsius, sed quia eius esse est causa τοῦ εἶναι omnium. Peccavisse igitur in eo omnes, non peccati ipsius imputatione, sed quia peccatum eius est causa peccati omnium; causa, inquam, eo modo quo ipsius esse est causa nostri, non imputationis divinae interventu, sed per generationem & propagationem naturalem.

pass_a.653: Placeus: the imputation you defend not only abolishes original vice—which still sits marrow-deep in every one of us, as Scripture and experience shout—but also undermines God’s φιλανθρωπία (love of mankind).
pass_a.654: Placeus presses the equity crack: God is made to will that Adam carry our person at the moment of the act, yet refuse that the same Adam still carry our person when the punishment falls.
pass_a.655: He treated Adam as our head when Adam sinned, but refused to treat him that way when Adam was being punished; he willed Adam to sin in our place, yet not to be punished in our place.
pass_a.656: He laid our persons on Adam so Adam would sin loco nostro, and in the same moment took them off lest Adam also be punished loco nostro—as if God delighted in the death of us who had ourselves done no sin, and by that person-imposition sought nothing from Adam but a pretext to make us all sinners.
pass_a.657: That you say Peter Martyr (who followed Calvin and Bucer and is wholly mine) and others granted that all sinned in Adam does not hurt Placeus: he cries that all sin in Adam as they die in Adam—by the force of communion with Adam, not by imputation of Adam’s singular sin or death.
pass_a.658: All sinned in Adam as they were in him. They were in him not by imputation of his being, but because his being causes the being of all. So they sinned in him not by imputation of his sin, but because his sin causes theirs—as his being causes ours—not by intervening divine imputation, but by natural generation and propagation.

653: Nor does the imputation you defend only take away original vice—which nevertheless is, alas, fixed marrow-deep in all and each of us, and Scripture cries out and experience bears witness—but it also undermines God’s φιλανθρωπία.
654: Seeing that he willed Adam to sustain our person when Adam sinned, but did not will that same man to sustain our person when Adam was punished.
655: He considered him our head when he sinned, and refused to consider him in the same way when he was being punished.
He willed him to sin in our place, and refused that he be punished in our place.
656: He imposed our persons on him so that he might sin in our place, and at the same moment took them away lest he likewise be punished in our place.

It is as if he had delighted in the death of us ourselves, who had ourselves sinned nothing, and by that imposition of our persons on Adam had sought nothing else than an occasion of making us all sinners.
657: That you say Peter Martyr (who followed the steps of Calvin and Bucer and is wholly mine) and the others acknowledged that all men sinned in Adam does not hurt me.
I cry that all men sin in Adam as they die in Adam—that is, by the force of the communion they have with Adam, not by imputation of his singular sin or of his death.
658: All men sinned in Adam as they were in him.
But they were in him not by imputation of his being (τοῦ εἶναι), but because his being is the cause of the being of all.

Therefore all sinned in him not by imputation of his sin, but because his sin is the cause of the sin of all—a cause, I say, in the same way his being is the cause of ours: not by intervening divine imputation, but through natural generation and propagation.
